source_text.coordinator_request: REVIEWER and SECURITY-REVIEWER must check the ADR's consistency with docs/migration/decisions/ especially 0002, 0006, 0035, 0038, 0042, 0043 and security-invariants INV-1..INV-8.

task.description: SECURITY gate on the PROPOSED decision record docs/migration/decisions/0044-hybrid-identity-model.md (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASS after 1 rework). It proposes a possible future shared-tier identity model (central realm, tenant selector, membership authorisation, domain-based routing) and a rollout whose Phase 1 is the already-ratified email-first directory. Review as a security design review: (a) the tenant-selector + membership rule and the INV-5 equivalence class (ADR 2.3.5): can a caller with a shared-realm account reach, read or be provisioned into a tenant they are not a member of; is 'JIT off for the shared realm' sufficient; what else could confer cross-tenant access (token claims, group/role mapping, subject collisions, email-verified/unverified emails, account linking, org membership vs local users row, deactivation propagation, token refresh)? (b) the weakening of 0006 s3.2 / R5 claims and 0002 'sole source' sentence: are the amendments honestly stated and bounded? (c) domain-based routing inference (R-7) and enumeration posture vs INV-5 and 0042 standing prohibitions (do the O3 additions keep the discovery response closed and byte-uniform?); (d) INV-1..INV-9 mapping in 2.3.7 and 6.7: is each correct against security-invariants.md (read the invariants file; quote the text you rely on); (e) anything the ADR should say but does not (e.g. account takeover via email change in the central realm, org-admin delegation, break-glass, audit trail per tenant, token audience/issuer pinning, logout/session scope, mobile token storage). Verify claims about this repo by reading the cited files (auth_pipeline.ex, identity.ex etc.). Do NOT edit the ADR. Output verdict RATIFIED/PASS or FAIL with findings classified BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR/ADVICE and exact locations; a FAIL means ORCH routes rework to CODE-DESIGNER. Note the ADR is PROPOSED and the user ratifies; your verdict is about security soundness and honesty of the record, not about choosing the option. Write the result into this handoff's 'result' (status PASS/FAIL, summary, issues[]) and set status COMPLETED; do not spawn agents; do not commit.
acceptance_criteria: INV-1..INV-9 mapping verified against security-invariants.md text

result.verdict: RATIFIED (security soundness and record honesty; the user ratifies the option)
result.summary: SECURITY-REVIEWER re-review of 0044 after rework 3 (commit 4afc2ca6): PASS / RATIFIED. 0 BLOCKER, 0 MAJOR, 0 MINOR, 1 ADVICE. N-1..N-5 are resolved in the text. N-1: 2.3.2 item 3 and R-7 now name the person-level inference (200 vs 202 reveals a single-tenant mailbox), the possible mail to nonexistent mailboxes for uniform tenants, and require dedupe by tenant in the joined query. N-2: 2.3.5 item 4b adds the ordering (explicit entry for every existing dedicated realm plus a boot check, then flip the fallback) or the alternative of scoping deny to shared realms. N-3: invitation transport is a URL fragment (`/invite#<token>`) in 2.3.1/2.3.2/2.3.8 item 4/6.3, token then sent only in a POST body. N-4: 2.2, 2.3.4 guarantee and (a)-(c) now say only an accepted invitation creates rows; the Phase 5 re-link tool is a separate, user-authorised writer bound to (realm, sub) pairs and never matches by e-mail. N-5: decoy defined as a real users lookup against a fixed existing tenant schema. Factual check of 4b: config/prod.exs:32-38 and config/dev.exs:137-143 list only bpm-default; config/test.exs:171-176 list bpm-default plus jit-disabled-test-realm (and further test realms); config/runtime.exs has no JIT or claim-mapping key; deploy/Dockerfile:6 sets MIX_ENV=prod so a deployed image (QA included) uses prod.exs; no env-based override of :oidc_jit_provisioning exists in the repository. So any QA realm other than bpm-default falls through JitProvisioningConfig.default/1 (enabled: true) provided it is bound as a tenant's idp_realm_id. The realm list itself (bilimbaga, swiftroute, meridian, vortex) is cited from the ai-dala-infra landscape doc outside this repository and the QA compose/env was not inspectable here; the ADR's wording is acceptable because it is conditioned by the boot check (every tenants.idp_realm_id must have an entry). Invitation transport coherence: a fragment is never sent to the SPA host or logs; the SPA POSTs the token in a body, so the INV-5 collapsed response for unknown/expired/used/revoked tokens (2.3.8 item 6), the first-plug limiter plus per-token attempt cap (item 5), the single tenant schema derived from the server-side token record (item 6) and the single writer (item 7) are unaffected and coherent; the Referrer-Policy and URL-replacement controls remain. New spike items S-17 (token lifetime/revocation) and S-18 (self-registration, email_verified, email edit, broker linking) honestly mark the previous assertions as ASSUMED/UNVERIFIED; no new contradictions found. Phase 0 text updated to S-1..S-18 consistently. Not a verdict on choosing O1/O2/O3.

issues.finding: The boot check 'every tenants.idp_realm_id has a JIT entry' covers realms bound at boot only; a tenant provisioned later at runtime would be denied until config is updated and the app restarted (JIT maps are compile/boot config). That is fail-closed and safe, but the Phase 2 runbook should say new dedicated realms need their entry before the tenant row is bound, or the map should move to per-tenant records (R-9).
